vt_high_grade_ledge.blurb: High Grade Ledge is a shelf of granite high on the right side of Marshfield Ledge in northern Vermont, sitting about two pitches above the ground. Its eleven routes are mostly steep, powerful sport lines, with most of them in the 5.13 range and a couple pushing into 5.14. A few trad climbs fill in the lower end, running from 5.7 up to 5.11. This is a place for strong climbers with endurance to spare rather than a beginner outing. Getting onto the ledge means either pulling up slab routes or jugging fixed lines, so expect some effort before the main climbing starts.

vt_area_51.blurb: Area 51 is a compact set of gneiss boulders in Bromley Forest, southern Vermont, just below the Crash Site boulders. The centerpiece is a big block leaning across a neighbor to form a cave, which is where the hard problems live. Eleven problems here split into two groups: six friendly ones from V0 to V2, and five much harder lines from V7 up to V12. There is little in the middle, so it suits strong boulderers and also works as a quick stop for easy circuits while exploring the surrounding Mothership boulders.

vt_thieves_wall.blurb: Thieves' Wall is a cliff band on a northern shoulder of Camel's Hump above Gleason Brook, in the Bolton area of Vermont. It faces west, so the lower sections stay shaded under tall trees and the wall picks up sun in the afternoon. The eleven routes are mostly trad, built on cracks and right-facing corners that take gear well, with two bolted sport lines mixed in. Grades run from 5.5 to 5.10, with the largest group around 5.7, making it a good fit for newer leaders and moderate trad climbers who want a quieter day.

vt_9_dometop.blurb: Dometop is the upper wall of Bolton Dome in northern Vermont, and one of the strongest faces in the Bolton area. It holds eleven routes, mostly bolted sport lines plus two trad climbs. Nearly all of the difficulty sits at 5.12, with one route near 5.9, one in the 5.10s and a pair of 5.11s. The lines are longer than they appear from below and finish at the top of the dome. Reach the wall by climbing fixed lines up to a ledge. It is a good objective for a climber with a solid 5.12 sport grade.
vt_9_dometop.parking_note: Leave the car in the small lot on Champ Lane, just off Route 2 at Bolton. It has room for roughly a dozen vehicles.

vt_kontos_traverse_boulder.blurb: The Kontos Traverse Boulder is one of the blocks at the Top of the Notch in Smugglers' Notch, northern Vermont, a short walk uphill from the parking area. It offers a gently overhanging face, an arete and a smooth, polished vertical side, giving eleven problems on schist. Grades start around V2 and climb to V12, with the bulk in the middle range of V4 to V10. The rock is slick, so it feels best in cool, dry weather and needs time to dry after rain or in humid heat.
